Thu Nov 19crypto

Binance wins $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order over October hack

The Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts issued a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order against the unidentified attackers behind Binance's Oct. 29 hack, the exchange and its lawyers at Gibson Dunn said, according to The Block and City AM. The order can be served through the blockchain and comes with a continuously updated list of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.

Thu Nov 19regulation

Appeals court rules 2-1 that Maryland can enforce its gambling laws against Kalshi

The US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit on Wednesday upheld a lower court's refusal to block Maryland from applying its sports-wagering laws to Kalshi's sports event contracts. It is the third of four federal appeals court decisions to side with state oversight of prediction markets, CoinDesk reported.

Thu Nov 19security

US launches Threat Disruption Center to stop scam payments after $20.9 billion in reported losses

The Homeland Security Task Force, co-led by the Homeland Security and Justice departments, launched a Threat Disruption Center to stop victims' money from reaching foreign scam, cybercrime and sextortion networks. It cited $20.9 billion in victim losses reported to the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center in 2025.

Thu Nov 19banking

Singapore issues S$100 million of tokenized central bank bills settled in wholesale CBDC

The Monetary Authority of Singapore said Thursday it issued S$100 million (about $77.5 million) of four-week tokenized MAS Bills on Nov. 6, created directly on its Singapore Dollar Test Network and settled in wholesale central bank digital currency.

Wed Nov 18markets

Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above its marketed range, reports say

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on Wednesday, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, according to Bloomberg, CNBC, Axios and the Associated Press.

Wed Nov 18policy

Fed minutes show almost all officials saw further rate hikes as likely appropriate

Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting, released Wednesday, show that almost all participants judged further increases in the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate to return inflation to 2%.

Wed Nov 18policy

Fed's Waller says a half-point rate hike is probably needed in December

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Wednesday that a half-percentage-point rate increase is probably needed at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless policymakers clearly signal another hike in January. He told CNBC that inflation is spreading and the Fed may need to "shock people."

Wed Nov 18economy

UK inflation rises to 3.6% in October, a one-year high, as diesel hits a record

UK consumer price inflation rose to 3.6% in the 12 months to October from 3.5% in September, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday. Motor fuels made the largest upward contribution.

Wed Nov 18crypto

World Bank Group to explore USDC stablecoin payments with Citi and Circle

The World Bank Group said on Tuesday it will work with Citi and Circle to explore whether regulated US dollar stablecoins can make its fund disbursements faster, cheaper and more transparent. Circle would mint and settle funds in USDC, while Citi would connect the effort to existing banking rails.

Wed Nov 18crypto

DBS lets institutional clients in Asia mint and redeem USDC directly, 24/7

DBS, Southeast Asia's largest bank by assets, said on Wednesday that eligible institutional clients can mint and redeem Circle's USDC stablecoin directly through the bank, with round-the-clock settlement between US dollars and USDC.

Tue Nov 17regulation

Kalshi halts Trump 'mention' markets after CFTC stay order

Prediction market Kalshi said on Tuesday it is complying with a Commodity Futures Trading Commission order that stayed its contracts on words President Donald Trump will say, after the regulator cited manipulation risk.

Tue Nov 17economy

US import prices rise 1.1% in October as capital goods post record gain

US import prices rose 1.1% in October, matching September's increase, as nonfuel import prices climbed 0.8%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Tuesday. Export prices also rose 1.1%.

Tue Nov 17regulation

CFTC approves Backpack to run a blockchain-based derivatives exchange and clearinghouse

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission designated TLD Markets, which does business as Backpack Exchange, as a designated contract market on November 16, three days after registering affiliate Backpack Clearing as a derivatives clearing organization. Chairman Michael Selig said the approvals show there is a regulated pathway for market infrastructure built on blockchain technology.

Mon Nov 16crypto

Judge acquits MIT-educated brothers in $25 million Ethereum trading case

A federal judge in Manhattan on Monday acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno of wire fraud and related conspiracy charges over a 2023 Ethereum trading strategy that netted about $25 million, a year after their trial ended in a hung jury.

Mon Nov 16markets

Fed Chair Warsh says AI will reshape the economy but could also 'disappoint'

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said Monday that AI "will have significant impact on the economy, with important implications for monetary policy down the road," in remarks to a Fed productivity and jobs task force in San Francisco.

Mon Nov 16crypto

Zelle picks Solana for its ZelleUSD stablecoin and international payments

Zelle said at the Breakpoint 2026 conference that its dollar-backed stablecoin, ZelleUSD, will launch on the Solana blockchain to support international peer-to-peer payments, Cointelegraph and Crypto Briefing reported.

Mon Nov 16regulation

Supreme Court rejects Custodia Bank's bid for a Fed master account

The Supreme Court on Monday denied Custodia Bank's petition for a writ of certiorari in Custodia Bank, Inc. v. Federal Reserve Board of Governors, No. 26-62, according to the Court's docket and its November 16 order list. The denial leaves in place a Tenth Circuit ruling that upheld the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's rejection of the Wyoming-chartered crypto bank's application for a master account.

Mon Nov 16economy

China industrial output slows to 4.8% in October; retail sales rise 0.4%

China's value added of industrial enterprises above designated size rose 4.8% year on year in October and retail sales of consumer goods rose 0.4%, the National Bureau of Statistics said, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in the first 10 months. CNBC reported that industrial output, retail sales and investment all missed economists' estimates, with industrial growth slowing from 5.5% in September.

Mon Nov 16economy

Japan's economy contracts at a 0.1% annualized rate in the third quarter

Japan's real GDP edged down 0.0% in the July-September quarter from the previous quarter, or 0.1% at an annualized rate, according to first preliminary estimates from the Cabinet Office, the first contraction in four quarters. Private consumption fell 0.3% and net exports subtracted 0.6 percentage points, while private non-residential investment rose 1.6%.

Mon Nov 16markets

DBS and J.P. Morgan start around-the-clock US-Singapore tokenized deposit transfers

DBS and Kinexys by J.P. Morgan said on Monday they have launched a service that lets institutional clients make instant US dollar transfers between blockchain-based accounts in the United States and Singapore, including on weekends. Ant International is the first client, the banks said in a DBS statement.

Sun Nov 15markets

Bessent says Nvidia needs a 'dramatic shake-up' and an outside CEO after Huang's exit

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that Nvidia's board should look outside the company for its next chief executive, after Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday.

Sat Nov 14crypto

Bitcoin slides to about $65,000, its lowest level since August

Bitcoin fell to around $65,000 on Saturday, its weakest level in about three months, extending a weekly drop of about 13.5%, CoinDesk reported.

Sat Nov 14markets

Two Nvidia investors urge the board not to rush a CEO pick and keep Huang's return open

Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker asked Nvidia's board in a public letter to run a "slow, measured, and deliberate" succession process that leaves open the potential return of Jensen Huang.

Fri Nov 13markets

Fed report: 87% of surveyed market contacts cite AI as a top financial-stability risk

The Federal Reserve's twice-yearly Financial Stability Report, released Friday, said 87% of market contacts in its fall survey cited artificial intelligence as a salient risk, up from 50% in the spring.

Fri Nov 13crypto

Kraken parent Payward's Q3 adjusted EBITDA rises to $60 million from Q2 but falls 66% from a year earlier

Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, reported third-quarter adjusted EBITDA of $60 million on Friday, up from $23 million in the second quarter but down 66% year over year, The Block reported.

Fri Nov 13economy

US producer prices rise 0.3% in October; annual rate 6.5%

The Producer Price Index (PPI) for final demand rose 0.3% in October after a 1.4% rise in September, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said, and the 12-month increase reached 6.5%, the largest since November 2022.

Fri Nov 13crypto

Bitcoin falls below $70,000 to 12-week low; $1.6B liquidated

Bitcoin dropped as low as $67,770 on Friday, its weakest level since August, as the dollar index climbed above 103 and leveraged long positions were forced out.

Fri Nov 13regulation

White House names four SEC and CFTC nominees

President Trump nominated Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine to the SEC and Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland to the CFTC, the first nominations to either agency in about a year.

Fri Nov 13regulation

DOJ and CFTC sue Arkansas to stop its Kalshi case

The Justice Department and the CFTC sued Arkansas in federal court on Thursday, asking a judge to block the state's Nov. 4 lawsuit accusing prediction market Kalshi of illegal gambling.

Thu Nov 12crypto

DOJ: North Korean deepfakes stole $400M crypto

The FBI seized infrastructure behind "FaceStealer" fake video calls, and DOJ won approval to seize or restrain over $1.2B from the Binance hack.

A Kalshi spokeswoman said the split opinions show there is no unified legal argument against prediction markets, CoinDesk reported. Details are in the court's opinion.
